BY THE BOARD: 
On July 1, 2024, and July 1, 2025, New Jersey’s electric distribution companies (”EDCs”) filed 
joint Basic Generation Service (“BGS”) proposals, including proposals to use a “descending clock” 
auction format to procure two-thirds of the State’s BGS requirements for Residential and Small 
Commercial Pricing (“BGS-RSCP”) customers.1 By Orders dated November 21, 2024, and 
November 21, 2025, the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (“Board” or “BPU”) approved the 
EDCs’ proposals, with modifications, for the period beginning June 1, 2027, and ending May 31, 
2028.2 The Auction Orders did not address procurement of the remaining one-third of BGS 
requirements for BGS-RSCP customers, or of the State’s annual BGS requirements for 
Commercial and Industrial Energy Pricing (“BGS-CIEP”) customers, for this period.3 
Additionally, prior Board Orders approved a process by which Rockland would procure its Central 
and Western Divisions’ energy and capacity needs from the New York Independent System 
1 The State’s four (4) investor-owned EDCs are Atlantic City Electric Company, Jersey Central Power & 
Light Company, Public Service Electric and Gas Company, and Rockland Electric Company (“Rockland”). 
2 In re the Provision of Basic Generation Service (BGS) for the Period Beginning June 1, 2025, BPU Docket 
No. ER24030191, Order dated November 21, 2024; In re the Provision of Basic Generation Service (BGS) 
for the Period Beginning June 1, 2026, BPU Docket No. ER25040190, Order dated November 21, 2025 
(collectively, “Auction Orders”). 
3 If the EDCs continue to propose a three (3) year rolling product as they have in prior filings, the BGS-
RSCP requirements procured for the period beginning June 1, 2026, will supply one-third of the BGS-RSCP 
load for the period June 1, 2026, through May 31, 2029.

Operator. Going forward, and to the extent not previously addressed by the Board, Rockland will 
need to address the procurement of its energy and capacity needs for those regions in its 
company-specific proposal. 

For twenty-five (25) years, the Board provided, through the BGS procurement process, an 
opportunity for all interested parties to participate through written comments, a legislative-type 
hearing, and public hearings. These procedures resulted in a wide range of suggestions, a timely 
Board decision, and ultimately, a successful procurement process each year. Accordingly, the 
Board intends to initiate a transparent proceeding to determine, for the period beginning June 1, 
2027, the best procurement process for BGS-RSCP and BGS-CIEP requirements, as well as 
Rockland’s non-PJM service area energy and capacity needs within New Jersey. This proceeding 
will include an invitation for all interested parties to propose how to procure BGS supply and an 
opportunity for all parties to issue discovery, provide written comments to the Board, and provide 
oral testimony at both a legislative-type and public hearings where the Board encourages the use 
of expert testimony. The proposed procedural schedule anticipates a Board decision on the 
process in November 2026, a BGS procurement process in February 2027, and a Rockland 
process for its non-PJM service area’s energy and capacity needs. 

As such, the Board HEREBY ORDERS the EDCs to file proposals no later than July 1, 2026, 
addressing how to procure the remaining one-third of the State’s BGS-RSCP requirements and 
the annual BGS-CIEP requirements for the period beginning June 1, 2027. The Board FURTHER 
ORDERS Rockland to file a proposal as part of its July 1, 2026, filing to procure the BGS energy 
and capacity requirements for its non-PJM service area within New Jersey for the period 
beginning June 1, 2027, to the extent not previously addressed. In addition, the Board invites all 
other interested stakeholders to file alternative BGS proposals with the Board by July 1, 2026. 

The Board HEREBY ADOPTS the preliminary procedural schedule attached hereto as 
Attachment A (“Schedule”), and the Board HEREBY ORDERS that all parties adhere to the 
Schedule unless otherwise directed by the Board. 

In compliance with the Board’s Orders in Docket No. EO20030254, all parties are HEREBY 
DIRECTED to serve all documents electronically.4 No hard copies shall be filed until the Board 
lifts the restrictions imposed in those Orders. The Board FURTHER DIRECTS that parties 
requesting to be added to the electronic service list email Stacy Peterson at 
stacy.peterson@bpu.nj.gov. 

4 In re the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities’ Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic for a Temporary 
Waiver of Requirements for Certain Non-Essential Obligations, BPU Docket No. EO20030254, Orders 
dated March 19, 2020, and June 10, 2020.
